mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 7 Series 740d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 7 Series 740d engine replacement typically costs £2,500-£4,500 for a used N57 or B57 unit, £3,800-£5,500 for a reconditioned engine, and £4,500-£7,000+ for a fully rebuilt engine with 12-month warranty. Supply and fit costs add approximately £800-£1,200 depending on your location and the specialist's labour rates.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of N57 or B57 engine failure in a BMW 7 Series 740d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs of N57 or B57 engine trouble in a 740d include: rattling noise from the engine bay at startup (timing chain stretch on N57 engines), loss of power and warning lights (DPF/EGR blockage), whistling noise during acceleration (turbocharger failure), oil spots under the car (valve cover or oil filter housing leaks), and increased fuel consumption.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 7 Series 740d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - if your BMW 7 Series 740d is otherwise in good condition, a replacement engine can extend its life significantly and retain strong value. With a typical 2016-2019 740d G11 valued at £15,000-£28,000, a rebuilt engine at £4,500-£7,000 plus fitting represents a sound investment for well-maintained examples.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 7 Series 740d engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most BMW 7 Series 740d engine replacements take 2-4 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. Collection and delivery options are available nationwide, with most engines dispatched within 24-72 hours of order confirmation.

mainEntity.name: Do BMW 7 Series 740d replacement engines come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all rebuilt BMW 7 Series 740d engines supplied through EnginesMarket include a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically come with a 3-6 month warranty depending on the supplier, and reconditioned engines often carry a 12-24 month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the N57 and B57 engines in the BMW 7 Series 740d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N57 (2008-2015) is BMW's previous-generation 3.0-litre diesel, available in twin-turbo configuration in the 740d. The B57 (2015-present) is BMW's modular replacement, featuring an aluminium alloy block, improved timing chain durability, and advanced emissions technology. B57 engines are generally more reliable and fuel-efficient, but both share common diesel-related issues like DPF and EGR clogging. The B57 also offers mild-hybrid options from 2020 onwards.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 7 Series 740d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 740d joined the 7 Series range as a 3.0-litre diesel option across two distinct generations: the F01 (2008-2015) and the G11/G12 (2015-2022). The 740d nameplate has been powered by two generations of BMW's straight-six diesel engines - the N57 and B57 families - making it one of the most technically advanced diesel badges in the 7 Series line-up. The B57 engine, introduced in 2015, replaced the previous N57 diesel engine and was first used in the G11 7 Series.

milestones.description: N57D30T0, 3.0L twin-turbo straight-six diesel, 306hp, launched with F01 740d
Facelift (LCI) updates across F01 range; N57D30T0 continues with revised emissions
B57D30T0, 3.0L twin-turbo straight-six diesel, 320hp, launched with G11/G12 740d
740d xDrive introduced with B57D30T0 and xDrive all-wheel drive
Facelift (LCI) updates across G11/G12 range; B57D30B (286hp) and B57D30C (340hp) variants introduced
B57D30C mild-hybrid variant introduced with 48V electrical system
G11/G12 production ends; 740d nameplate continues into G70 generation

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 7 Series 740d is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 7 Series 740d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 7 Series 740d has been powered by two generations of BMW's 3.0-litre straight-six diesel - the N57 (2008-2015) and B57 (2015-2022). Replacement demand for the 740d is dominated by the N57D30T0 and B57D30 variants, with timing chain failure (particularly on N57 engines), DPF/EGR clogging, turbocharger issues, and oil leaks being the most frequent drivers of replacement decisions. Rebuilt BMW 7 Series 740d engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why the BMW 7 Series 740d N57 Engine Suffers Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Timing chain issues in N57 engines are often due to tensioner wear and chain stretch over time. Symptoms include metallic rattling noise from the engine at startup, rough idling, and engine misfires. If the chain fails, valves collide with pistons, causing catastrophic engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioners, and guides
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early before catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing chain components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if chain failure has caused valve/piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2010-2013 BMW 7 Series 740d F01 is valued between £6,000 and £13,000 depending on condition and mileage. For vehicles worth £10,000+, a rebuilt engine at £4,500-£5,800 plus fitting is financially viable. For cars at the lower end of the value spectrum (under £6,000), a used engine or scrappage may be the more sensible choice.
problems.recommendation: If you hear rattling from the engine bay at startup, have the timing chain inspected immediately. Early intervention with a chain and tensioner replacement (£1,500-£2,200 at a specialist) can prevent catastrophic engine failure. If the chain has already failed and damaged the engine, a rebuilt unit is the only sensible path forward.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N57D30T0 BMW 7 Series 740d engine prices

problems.h4: DPF and EGR System Clogging - Why the BMW 7 Series 740d Diesel Suffers
problems.rootCause: Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) blockage occurs when the vehicle is frequently driven on short trips that do not allow the engine to reach the temperatures needed for DPF regeneration. The Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) valve becomes clogged with carbon deposits over time. Symptoms include loss of power, poor fuel economy, warning lights, and failed MOT emissions tests.

repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if DPF is partially blocked

problems.recommendation: If your 740d's DPF or EGR system is causing issues, start with a forced regeneration or professional cleaning (£100-£800 at a specialist). If the vehicle has high mileage (80,000+) and the DPF and EGR are both heavily clogged, a full rebuilt engine with cleaned systems may offer better long-term value than piecemeal repairs.

problems.h4: Turbocharger and Oil Leak Issues - Why the BMW 7 Series 740d Suffers
problems.rootCause: Turbocharger failure can occur due to oil starvation, which may be caused by clogged oil passages or insufficient oil changes. Oil leaks are one of the most common issues on the B57 engine, often originating from the valve cover gasket or oil filter housing. Symptoms include loss of power, whistling noise during acceleration, engine light illumination, stalling at idle, and increased fuel consumption.

problems.recommendation: If your 740d has lost power and is making a whistling noise, have the turbocharger inspected immediately. A specialist rebuild (£900-£1,500) is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Similarly, address oil leaks promptly - ignoring them can lead to low oil levels and severe engine damage.
